module_name: Static Code Analysis / Androguard-based APK Disassembly + APG Construction
responsibility: Given an Android .apk, disassemble it (Dalvik bytecode via androguard) and emit an App Property Graph (APG) â€” four intertwined views: AST (Method/Statement structure), MCG (method call graph), ICFG (intra-procedural next-statement control flow), and DDG (data-dependence between register-writing and register-reading statements). This is Stage 1-2 of the pipeline: it produces the {AST,MCG,ICFG,DDG}_{nodes,edges}.csv schema that Stage 4 (PPG) consumes. The in-memory APG (classes, methods, statements, has_method, has_statement, calls, icfg_next, data_depends) is defined once in pplib/apg_model.py and shared by every downstream stage.
research_role: Stage 1-2 of the APK â†’ APG â†’ PPG â†’ PRCS â†’ PAcT â†’ Model â†’ Caption pipeline. Emits the AST/MCG/ICFG/DDG that everything else (PPG overlay, taint propagation, PRCS slicing, ConvGNN featurization) is built on. The disassembly + APG-construction logic lives in `adapters/run_apg_csv.py`; the in-memory dataclass and CSV read/write contract lives in `pplib/apg_model.py`. `pplib/schema.py` freezes the node/edge column names (APG_NODE_COLUMNS, APG_EDGE_COLUMNS) that both the legacy script and the adapter must obey so downstream stages don't care which produced them.

Concretely: (1) `pplib/apg_model.py` loads the four Stage 2 CSV pairs (AST/MCG/ICFG/DDG) into an in-memory APG and reconstructs Class + HAS_METHOD (which Stage 2 only writes to Neo4j); (2) `stage4_ppg/catalogs.py` classifies each APG Statement's callee as a PI Source (3 tiers: curated `known_sources`, SuSi `formatted_sources.csv`, and NL enrichment from Stage 3 `personal_info_results.csv`) or a Sink (rule catalog `configs/sinks.yaml` + unknown-sink egress-verb heuristic); (3) `stage4_ppg/taint.py` runs a BFS taint propagation over DATA_DEPENDS (+ optional ICFG_NEXT) with two inter-procedural rules (CALL-ARG: invoke-of-internal-method -> callee entry stmt; CALL-RET: a method that ever holds taint -> its call sites) capped by `max_depth`, `dedup_by_method`, `max_paths_per_source`; (4) `stage4_ppg/build_ppg.py` (`PPGBuilder`) copies the APG structure, adds overlay nodes (Source, Sink, DataItem, Store, Component) and overlay edges (TAINT_FLOW + PRIVACY_RELATION with sub-relation ACCESSES / OF_TYPE / WRITES_TO / PERSISTS_IN / SENDS_VIA / FLOWS_TO), tags each flow with LINDDUN-GO threats from `configs/ppg.yaml:linddun_map` (plus `Identifying` escalation for identifying PI categories), writes overlay props back onto Statement nodes, and finally invokes `semantics.enrich_graph` to attach a rule-based (or optional LLM) `what_it_does` to every node; (5) optional `neo4j_loader.py` upserts the whole graph into Neo4j and `cypher_runner.py` renders/executes the `configs/queries.cypher` library.

gaps_or_issues: Heuristic taint is intentionally an over-approximation: DDG + ICFG + a coarse CALL-RET rule that marks EVERY call site of any tainted method as tainted (`succ.extend(callsites.get(m, []))` in taint.py) â€” README Â§Findings explicitly flags this; precision knobs (`follow_icfg:false`, `max_paths_per_source:25`) exist and pipeline/run_pipeline.py exposes `--precision` to switch them on, but the default config still uses the recall-oriented settings.

Sink classification is called twice per statement in build_ppg.py:104-122 (once for the source/sink precedence decision, then `self.sinks.classify(callee)` re-runs immediately after `continue`) â€” wasteful on large APKs but not incorrect.

Sanity-only unit-test coverage: only `tests/test_stage4_ppg.py` (7 tests over adapter, catalogs, and one integration on a synthetic fixture) plus `tests/test_neo4j_display.py` â€” no tests exercise real SuSi/personal_info CSVs, the LINDDUN escalation branch, the `formatted_match_by_method_name` recall mode, or the WhatItDoesCache eviction/reload paths.

GraphML export must strip XML-illegal control characters from decompiled smali (`_xml_safe` in build_ppg.py) and still catches all exceptions; failures are logged as a warning and the pipeline continues with pickle only â€” no metric surfaced when this happens on real APKs.

The Neo4j path is genuinely optional but the ONLY visualization: `neo4j_loader.py` and the `--neo4j`/`--run` flags require an external server and the `neo4j` Python package; there is no built-in offline visualizer (only the Cypher-render mode of cypher_runner).

`pplib/apg_model.py:load_apg` bulk-reads all four CSVs into pandas DataFrames then materializes every row into Python dicts; on the 10,721-PRCS real corpus this is the memory bottleneck (no streaming/iter_rows path).

`known_sources` in configs/ppg.yaml is a hand-curated list (~16 APIs) â€” sources of coverage/precision limits acknowledged only in README, not in the code; no test asserts that every category listed in `permission_map` has at least one signature.

Provenance is retained for descriptions (`what_it_does_src` = 'rule' | 'llm:<provider>' in semantics.py) and per-node `app_id` + sink `known` flag + source `tier`, but there is NO per-edge provenance on TAINT_FLOW: the flow does not record whether it came from DDG-only, ICFG, CALL-ARG, or CALL-RET traversal, so downstream consumers cannot filter by taint-rule strength.

`_idx(stmt_id)` in taint.py silently returns 0 when a statement id does not match the `{method}_stmt_{i}` convention, so method-entry selection can be wrong for adapters that use a different id format â€” no assertion in load_apg.

The heuristic sink verb list overlaps with common non-egress verbs (e.g. `log`, `put`, `save`) and, combined with the CALL-RET taint rule, is the acknowledged source of the flow explosion on real APKs (per docs/FINDINGS.md Â§ referenced by ppg.yaml comments).

gaps_or_issues: PRCS schema is defined only implicitly by the PRCS @dataclass and INDEX_COLUMNS list in extract_prcs.py â€” no versioned JSON schema file (e.g. pplib/schema.py has label constants but no PRCS field spec), so downstream consumers rely on ad-hoc key names.

Subgraph is capped at CONTEXT_HOPS=1 and MAX_SUBGRAPH_NODES=150 as hard-coded module constants (not surfaced in configs/ or CLI); silently truncates real-app slices without a warning or a truncated=True flag on the record.
_idx() falls back to 0 for any statement id not matching '_stmt_<int>', which can silently break ordering of _method_statements if PPG naming ever changes; no defensive test.

code_snippet is a flat text render (`// <method_id>` header + '  <code>' lines); if a PPG node has neither 'code' nor 'type', the line becomes blank and the snippet loses fidelity â€” no test asserts non-empty snippet content per line.

_stable_id truncates the SHA-1 to 12 hex chars; collision-safe at current corpus scale (~10k PRCS) but not proven, and no collision check is performed when writing per-PRCS JSON (a duplicate id would silently overwrite prcs_<id>.json).

Provenance is preserved via {app_package, apk_filename, class_name, method_name, method_signature, source_api, sink_api, involved_methods} on the record and a `provenance` block in the Codr export â€” but the taint_path itself (the ordered node ids the slice came from) is NOT stored on the PRCS, so you cannot reconstruct which nodes in `subgraph` lay on the flow vs. which are neighborhood context.

Weak labeler purpose detection is a simple str.startswith on class names against configs/sdk_catalog.yaml lists (advertisement / analytics); obfuscated or shaded SDKs will be missed silently, and there is no coverage metric on how many PRCS get the default 'Functionality' purpose because no SDK matched.

_grouped_splits has fragile rounding for tiny group counts: with 2 groups, n_val=1 forces train/val but leaves test empty then rescues by popping from val/train â€” behaviour only exercised implicitly by the 8-app fixture; no unit test covers 1/2/3-group edge cases.

build_dataset writes one JSON per PRCS into codr_export/ with no pagination or manifest; on the 10,721-PRCS corpus this produces 10k+ small files, mirroring the same shape as data/prcs/ (see next item).
